---
title: "Releases"
---

Images are published to the GitHub Container Registry as
`ghcr.io/kf8eez/graywolf-container` (GHCR requires a lowercase name). Releases
are made with `scripts/publish.sh`.

## Tags

A release is named `YYYY-MM-DD-NN`, where `NN` is a serial number for that day
(`01`, `02`, ...), so several releases on one day never collide.

| Tag                   | Contents                                              |
|-----------------------|-------------------------------------------------------|
| `2026-11-14-01-amd64` | amd64 image only                                      |
| `2026-11-14-01-arm64` | arm64 image only                                      |
| `2026-11-14-01`       | multi-arch manifest: pulls the right image for the host |
| `latest`              | multi-arch manifest of the newest release             |
| `gw-0.14.14`          | multi-arch manifest of the newest release built with graywolf 0.14.14 |

`latest` and `gw-<version>` are moved to each new release. The release tag is
permanent: the script refuses to overwrite an existing tag. The image label
`org.opencontainers.image.revision` records the git commit of every build.

Pull a specific release, or pin one in compose:

```bash
podman pull ghcr.io/kf8eez/graywolf-container:2026-11-14-01
GRAYWOLF_TAG=2026-11-14-01 podman compose up -d
```

## Publishing a release

Each architecture is built natively on its own machine (an amd64 PC and a
Raspberry Pi 5), so no emulation is needed. Run from a clean, pushed checkout
of the same commit on both machines.

**One-time login (each machine).** The token needs the `write:packages` scope,
and your GitHub account must be allowed to create packages in the `KF8EEZ`
organization.

```bash
gh auth refresh -s write:packages
gh auth token | podman login ghcr.io -u "$(gh api user -q .login)" --password-stdin
```

**1. Build and push the first architecture.** With no tag given, the script
asks the registry for today's existing tags and uses the next serial. It prints
the tag it chose.

```bash
scripts/publish.sh amd64            # on the PC
```

**2. Build and push the other architecture** with the same tag.

```bash
scripts/publish.sh arm64 2026-11-14-01    # on the Pi 5
```

**3. Publish the multi-arch tags,** from either machine. This checks that both
architecture tags exist, then pushes `2026-11-14-01`, `latest` and
`gw-<graywolf version>`.

```bash
scripts/publish.sh manifest 2026-11-14-01
```

Add `--dry-run` to any command to print what would happen without building or
pushing. `scripts/publish.sh next` prints the next free tag.
`IMAGE=ghcr.io/kf8eez/some-test-name scripts/publish.sh ...` publishes to a
different package, which is useful for a trial run.

## First publish

New GHCR packages are private. After the first push, open the package settings
on GitHub, link it to the repository, and change its visibility to public so
`podman compose up` can pull it without logging in. Until the first release is
published there is no image to pull; use `compose.build.yaml` to build locally.
